title: Opening the Unopenable Skull — Harvey Cushing's Mortality Collapse (>50–80% to <8%) via Riva-Rocci Cuff, Ether Charts, Silver Clips (1911), William Bovie's 1926 Electrosurgery & Louise Eisenhardt's >2,200-Tumor Registry, the Feud With Walter Dandy (1918 Ventriculography), Cushing Reflex (CPP = MAP - ICP), Minnie G.'s Pituitary Basophilism & ACTH–MC2R–MRAP1 / MR / 11β-HSD1 (PDB 8GY7, 2AA2, 2A3I, 1Y5R)

teenKit.tldr: In 1900, brain surgery was an execution notice with an 80% death rate, but pioneering surgeon Harvey Cushing and modern tools transformed it into a precise, life-saving science.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Without these grueling surgical breakthroughs and molecular discoveries, conditions that we can now easily treat with a routine operation would still be instant death sentences.
keyTakeaways: Early 20th-century brain surgery was a terrifying bloodbath using mallets and chisels with a mortality rate between 50% and 80%.
Harvey Cushing revolutionized the field by introducing real-time blood pressure monitoring, silver clips to stop bleeding, and meticulous record-keeping via Dr. Louise Eisenhardt.
The journey of neurosurgery stretches from brutal blind operations all the way down to atomic-level hormone interactions that dictate human metabolism.

vocab.meaning: A physiological response where a dangerous spike in pressure inside the skull triggers a massive surge in blood pressure and slows the heart rate.
An early medical imaging technique where air was injected directly into the brain's ventricles so tumors would show up on X-rays.
The use of high-frequency electrical currents by inventor William Bovie to simultaneously cut tissue and seal bleeding blood vessels.
A hormonal disorder caused by a tiny tumor in the pituitary gland that triggers severe, cascading changes in body chemistry and metabolism.

quiz.question: What was the approximate operative mortality rate for brain surgery around the year 1900?
quiz.explanation: Opening the skull in 1900 was so dangerous and primitive that 50% to 80% of patients died on the table or shortly after.

quiz.question: Who was Harvey Cushing's fiercely unsung partner that managed the massive tumor registry and neurosurgical collection?
quiz.explanation: Dr. Louise Eisenhardt was the indispensable partner who curated over 2,200 tumor cases and built the world-class brain registry.

quiz.question: What technological innovation did William Bovie introduce to the operating room in 1926 that changed neurosurgery forever?
options: High-frequency electrosurgery for cutting and sealing blood vessels
quiz.explanation: Bovie's electrosurgery unit allowed surgeons to slice through tissue while instantly zapping and sealing bleeding vessels to prevent massive blood loss.
